name: The signed-in competitor
description: The join on live_sessions is the revocation check, and it is a join rather than a guard task so it costs no extra round trip and cannot be omitted by mistake. It yields no row for a session that has been signed out -- or for a valid token whose user has been deleted -- and `deny` refuses that case first: a condition-gated terminal task is how a workflow refuses a request while choosing its own status, and it has to be 401 because the shell maps 401 to anonymous and every other status to an error panel. (`halt_on: "failure"`, new in Orion 1.6, would stop the run but answer 400.) Postgres builds the response: the `body` column is json_build_object, and since Orion 1.6 a json column decodes as the document itself, so the respond task copies it into data.body.

input.query: SELECT json_build_object('id', u.id, 'handle', u.handle, 'role', u.role) AS body FROM users u JOIN live_sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id AND s.sid = ($2)::uuid WHERE u.id = ($1)::uuid
